input.cause: At the time of the two tasks, the procedure brief (specs/procedure/words.json /brief/safetyBounds) said to cite "the fact" its signed rules bound a constant by, and the safety card said to cite "the fact's id as its reference". Neither said that the reference must be exactly one id. The model joined two ids, e.g. "test.speedFloorPercent; scrubber.effectiveFlowAtFull 1 m3/min (scrubber-1-datasheet)". The guard refused this with "is not a fact of the library". That wording does not say that one id alone is accepted. At the first retry the model kept only test.speedFloorPercent and replaced the value, so the correction is "reference narrowed, value replaced". The gap was in the texts, and the models only learned the rule by being refused. The phrase "by its id alone as the reference" has been added to /brief/safetyBounds, and justify.ts now says "Exactly one: for library, one id". Both are stated today, so the gap is closed.

input.summary: Diagnosis diag-d51a49a86fed accepted by the guard. The lead (D2:8cba194716f8) is right and its class is contract-gap. The refusals in task:exp3-baseline/t-2026-09-29-0010 (step 8) and task:exp4-sonnet-a/t-2026-09-29-0008 (step 9) both fall under REFERENCE_NOT_A_FACT. In both, the model joined two ids in one reference, for example "test.speedFloorPercent; scrubber.effectiveFlowAtFull 1 m3/min (scrubber-1-datasheet)". The guard accepts one fact id and nothing else. The safety card said to cite "the fact's id as its reference", and the model read that as allowing several ids. The retry narrowed the reference to test.speedFloorPercent and replaced the value (100 became 30), the first-retry pattern the lead counts. The harness confirmed that at the tasks' version (4e3458b) safetyBounds did not hold the "single fact, by its id alone" wording. It also confirmed that this wording is stated today in specs/procedure/words.json#/brief/safetyBounds and in harness/core/justify.ts, and that test.speedFloorPercent = 30 percent is a signed fact in commissioning-test-safety. So the cause is closed since 287f5bc and nothing is left to recommend.
